questions.q: How did ITIL v3 (2007, refreshed 2011) organize its guidance?
options: Around a Service Lifecycle of five stages — Strategy, Design, Transition, Operation, and Continual Service Improvement — containing 26 processes
Around 34 practices grouped into three categories
Around a single Service Value Chain with six activities
It had no structural organization at all
questions.explain: ITIL v3 reorganized earlier process books into a five-stage Service Lifecycle containing a defined set of 26 processes.

questions.q: What limitation of the ITIL v3 lifecycle model does this lesson identify?
options: It had too many lifecycle stages to be useful
It modeled service delivery as a largely linear, sequential flow, with no real vocabulary for the Agile and DevOps practices organizations were adopting
It completely ignored the idea of continual improvement
It required no documentation at all
questions.explain: The sequential strategize-then-design-then-transition structure didn't map cleanly onto the continuous, iterative delivery that Agile and DevOps use.

questions.q: Why did ITIL 4 replace the term "process" with "practice"?
options: It was a purely cosmetic rebranding with no functional difference
A practice is a set of organizational resources — including people, skills, and tools — designed for performing work, which is broader than a sequence of steps
"Practice" was chosen because it sounds more modern, with no definitional change
Practices replaced processes because ITIL 4 removed workflow guidance entirely
questions.explain: The rename reflects a genuinely broader definition: a practice includes the people, skills, and tools involved, not just the workflow steps.

questions.q: What does ITIL 4's four dimensions model require when evaluating any practice or service?
options: Considering only the technology dimension, since that's what IT is primarily about
Considering organizations and people, information and technology, partners and suppliers, and value streams and processes, all at once
Considering four separate certification exams
Considering only financial cost and nothing else
questions.explain: The four dimensions model forces a holistic view beyond process steps alone — who does the work, what information and tools they need, external partners, and the end-to-end flow.

questions.q: How does ITIL 4 treat Agile, DevOps, and Lean compared to ITIL v3?
options: ITIL 4 explicitly incorporates Agile, DevOps, and Lean thinking into its guidance, which ITIL v3 did not address
ITIL 4 removed all mention of Agile, DevOps, and Lean
ITIL v3 already fully incorporated Agile and DevOps guidance before ITIL 4 existed
Agile, DevOps, and Lean are unrelated to any version of ITIL
questions.explain: ITIL v3 predates the widespread adoption of Agile/DevOps practices in its original form; ITIL 4 was written to explicitly embrace them.
